rulings.status: supersedes 2.1:G46; supersedes the in-place clause of 0.8:G4
rulings.rule: A ki-word may open the clause or stay where its answer would stand; the album fronts it in most questions. A yes/no question must end in ki. A question with a ki-word may end in ki or not. Embedded wh-questions may also front the ki-word and never end in ki; embedded yes/no questions use ki-oro (1.0:G2).
examples: maivori ne sabesia ki-coda maivori ramura.

rulings.rule: Only ki-modo + adjective, ki-eli + noun and ki-muya + noun make an exclamation, and only when the clause does not end in ki. Any other ki-word clause without ki is a question. A degree question (ki-modo + adjective) must end in ki.
examples: Li nullo ka ki-modo vanisan ki?

rulings.rule: tonsi directly before an adjective means “so”; a following fime clause gives the result. Clause-initial tonsi keeps its meaning “therefore”.
examples: taivo ke tonsi corvisan fime taivo viki savalisia maivo ki?
si maivo ke tonsi lukasan, maivo futu ne salrusia.

rulings.rule: After a main clause, a fime clause whose verb carries nosi means “in the hope that, so that perhaps”. kopisa stays the plain purpose linker.
examples: maivo futu donuda ito biti de lalfo, fime taivo nosi semnesia ko maivo en moluvaye.

rulings.rule: raho with no noun before it means “the one who, that which”, as subject, object or complement. raho is never a question word: questions use ki-nela or ki-coda.
examples: saivo po farufasbifa kube saivo ramura raho maivo po ke.

rulings.rule: An adjective may take sidu + verb for “easy to …, ready to …”. The verb’s object is what the adjective describes.
examples: ito ke ruli levasan sidu zeldoza trana.

rulings.topic: kroti and krotiapo before a clause
rulings.rule: kroti and krotiapo may introduce a clause: “before …”, “after …”. The clause inherits tense like kube (0.8:R6). Before a measure they keep 2.1:G55; before li + noun, their 2.0 meaning.
examples: kroti maivo lesvu taivo ke li sevusan ruhe.

rulings.rule: nazru (behind), zavme (in front of), silda (beside), cemnu (in the middle of), lizma (left of) and rizno (right of) may stand bare before a noun phrase as prepositions, or after a verb as adverbs.
examples: Li lavra semnesia nazru li nimu.
saivo de melonulu venreva nazru gase baba lira de ruhesonbu.

rulings.rule: The album (twelve songs and the alternate 05) is canon 2.0 text, read with 2.0 spellings under 2.1:G58. A construction it uses consistently is grammar. A line that departs from the grammar once is an album reading: it keeps its intended meaning, is listed with its standard form, and is not a model for new text.

album_readings.recorded: lanto, saivo po veseva fime raho saivo viki ke saivo de devorivo.
album_readings.issue: fime + headless raho has no predicate for the raho-phrase.
album_readings.standard_form: lanto, saivo po veseva fime saivo viki ke saivo de devorivo.
album_readings.note: Probable intent: drop raho (“whispered that he would be her betrothed”). Confirm with the author.

album_readings.recorded: maivo po ke baba lirasan lavra norusan.
album_readings.standard_form: maivo po ke baba norusan lirasan lavra.

album_readings.recorded: li linu raho navdinia sabesia baba bio de milno.
album_readings.issue: Relative clause not closed by a comma (1.0:G21).
album_readings.standard_form: li linu raho navdinia, sabesia baba bio de milno.

album_readings.recorded: maivo mambivimoma ala li ata masuma lanla ata po milobema.
album_readings.issue: li followed directly by ata; the phrase does not parse.
album_readings.note: Author to supply the intended line.

album_readings.recorded: kube ito futu ke salrusan maivo ata donuda ala ito baba biti vobi demro.
album_readings.issue: Appears to be a draft of the next line, which says the same thing correctly.
album_readings.note: Author to confirm whether the recorded vocal uses this line.

album_readings.recorded: voyu taivo de navu maivo ne povi navdinia maivo.
album_readings.standard_form: voyu taivo de navu maivo ne povi navdinia maivo sela.

album_readings.recorded: maivo futu senosia ala taivo de baba gargonasan colbi.
album_readings.issue: Pronoun + de reads as owner (1.2:G27): “your gentle colour”. Recipient order is VERB THEME ala RECIPIENT (1.2:G26).
album_readings.standard_form: maivo futu senosia baba gargonasan colbi ala taivo.

album_readings.recorded: maivo futu veseva ala taivo de li vera de damruna.
album_readings.issue: Same pronoun + de issue as the line above.
album_readings.standard_form: maivo futu veseva li vera de damruna ala taivo.

album_readings.recorded: li sabeasasan nelari raho pensapa peburalno en milno ki?
album_readings.issue: peburalno is the noun; the verb is peburalnopa. Relative needs a closing comma.
album_readings.standard_form: li sabeasasan nelari raho pensapa, peburalnopa en milno ki?

album_readings.recorded: si maivo ke sidu daigoda, maivo kopi daigoda en saivo de varori.
album_readings.issue: sidu never follows a copula (1.0 linking rule).
album_readings.standard_form: si maivo musi daigoda, maivo kopi daigoda en saivo de varori.
album_readings.note: Held question: ke sidu VERB as “destined to” (see open_questions).

album_readings.recorded: maivo po silbesia saivo de vaye raho po jubaja baba nonmori.
album_readings.issue: Pronoun + de reads as owner: “her wind”.
album_readings.standard_form: maivo po silbesia saivo baba vaye raho po jubaja baba nonmori.
album_readings.note: Use the standard form only if “her” was meant as the recipient.

album_readings.recorded: tonsi maivo po silbesia saivo de baba pagonasan folni.
album_readings.issue: Pronoun + de before baba reads as owner; recipient takes VERB PRONOUN THEME (1.2:G26).
album_readings.standard_form: tonsi maivo po silbesia saivo baba pagonasan folni.

album_readings.recorded: maivo po veseva ala saivo de li krotiata lirasarbi.
album_readings.issue: Pronoun + de reads as owner: “her next poem”.
album_readings.standard_form: maivo po veseva li krotiata lirasarbi ala saivo.

album_readings.recorded: saivo po farufasbifa kube saivo ramusan raho maivo po ke.
album_readings.issue: ramusan is the adjective (“memorable”); the verb is ramura. Headless raho is canon from 2.2:G64.
album_readings.standard_form: saivo po farufasbifa kube saivo ramura raho maivo po ke.

album_readings.recorded: maivo toda-krono po ke saivo de devorivo.
album_readings.issue: A time word stands first or last (1.2:G24), not between subject and tense.
album_readings.standard_form: maivo po ke saivo de devorivo toda-krono.

album_readings.recorded: raho povi sabesia baba kasi polvasan sove ki?
album_readings.issue: raho is relative only; the question word is ki-nela.
album_readings.standard_form: ki-nela povi sabesia baba kasi polvasan sove ki?

add: ke sidu VERB as “destined to” (album 08); hold until a second use.
Relatives with a gap for time or place (album 01: krono raho …); hold until a second use.

edition_note: Liraasa 2.2 added rulings 2.2:G60–G68, restored the 2.0 spelling silro (reverting the 2.1 respelling puzu), filled the forms soloasa and tarnulinusan, and added the album as the reference corpus with sixteen album readings.
